fix(vite): drop min_viewport_width from inline manifest

vite-plugin-pwa types reject unknown manifest fields (TS2353) and
min_viewport_width is platform-custom, not standard PWA. orientation
stays — it's a real PWA field. The central viewport-support check

fix(compliance): declare orientation + --bg token

Two pre-existing central-compliance gaps that have been failing the
"Viewport support" and "Brand tokens defined" checks for the whole
game catalog:

- web/vite.config.ts inline PWA manifest now declares
  `orientation: "any"` and `min_viewport_width: 360`, so the storefront
  coverage badge has values to display and the central viewport-support
  check passes.
- web/src/index.css now defines `--bg` as an alias of `--paper`, so the
  brand-tokens check sees the game token (`--bg`) it expects for games.
  Existing rules using `var(--paper)` keep working unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mp): on rejected move, server sends state-snapshot so client can rollback

Two adjacent issues:

1. Client does an optimistic local chess.move() before sending to the
   server (snappy UX). If the server rejects the move (race condition:
   opponent's move arrived first), the client only gets `{type: error}`
   and never rolls back. Result: client board ahead of true state.

2. Rematch (type=new_game) handler on the client didn't clear
   selectedSquare or stale errors, so the new game inherited cursor +
   error state from the previous one.

Fix:
- Server: extract a sendState() helper. After rejecting a move
  ('Illegal', 'Not your turn', 'Game is over'), send a fresh state
  snapshot to just that client. Client already handles `type: state`
  via chess.load(fen), so optimistic moves silently roll back.
- Client: on new_game, also clear selectedSquare + error.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mp): show "Opponent Resigned · You Won!" instead of "You Resigned" to the winner

GameOverBanner had a hard-coded "You Resigned" message for any
status='resigned' game-over, regardless of WHICH side resigned. In MP,
when the opponent resigned, the winner's banner also said "You Resigned"
— factually wrong and confusing.

Now branches on the playerLost prop the parent already computes
correctly: my-resign → "You Resigned", opponent-resign → "Opponent
Resigned · You Won!".

PlayTab (single-player) only resigns via the player's own voice
command, so playerLost is always true there. No regression.

Found by /qa with two browser tabs in a fresh MP game.

Billiards: fix 3 bugs in the archery aim model

- Cue stick rendered FORWARD of the cue ball at low power. The math
  `(BALL_R + 4 + pullback - 36)` produced a NEGATIVE offset until
  pullback ≥ 28 — so at 0% the tip was on the aim-line side instead
  of behind the ball. Replaced with `baseGap + pullback` so the tip
  is always behind the ball, just farther back as power rises.

- SHOOT button fired the shot if your finger drifted off it mid-hold.
  `onPointerLeave={() => releaseCharge()}` triggered on common mobile
  slip. Replaced with `setPointerCapture` on press so the button keeps
  receiving events until pointerup, and pointercancel now drops the
  charge silently instead of firing.

- Ball-in-hand placement could drop the cue ball INSIDE another ball
  (no overlap check). Added a 24-pass nudge that pushes the cue ball
  away from any overlapped ball until clear, clamped to the cushion.

Billiards: switch to archery-style aim (hold to charge, release to fire)

Replaces the drag-from-cue-ball gesture with a separate aim/power model:

- Aim: pointer position on the canvas sets the aim line; no firing on
  pointer-up. Move freely to fine-tune the angle.
- Power: dedicated SHOOT button below the canvas. Hold down → power
  charges over ~715ms to full. Release → fires (or cancels if released
  below 8% — accidental taps don't lose your turn).
- Visual: a cue stick now renders behind the cue ball and pulls back
  proportionally to the charging power, with blue chalk tip + wood
  shaft + dark butt. The power ring around the cue ball turns red
  near max for a wind-up warning.
- Keyboard: ← → still adjusts angle; Space (hold + release) replaces
  the old "tap Space to fire instantly" with charge-and-release.
- Ball-in-hand: tap-anywhere placement still works; shoot button is
  disabled with explicit "TAP TABLE TO PLACE CUE" label.

fix: aim direction now matches spin direction

After flipping spin to camera-natural ("drag right = curve right"),
the AIM phase was left with the inverse mapping: dragging right or
pressing ArrowRight moved the ball to the camera-LEFT, because aimX
was still naive (positive = +X = camera-left in Babylon's left-handed
coords with the camera looking down -Z).

Same gesture, opposite effect across two adjacent phases — confusing.

Flipped both the drag delta (×-0.015 instead of ×+0.015) and the arrow
keys (ArrowLeft now +=, ArrowRight now -=) so all aim/spin controls
agree: right input = camera-right ball motion. aimX still represents
the ball's true world-X position, which keeps the render code clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(types): add @types/node so compliance test type-checks

The compliance test imports node:fs / node:path / __dirname. Without
@types/node in web's devDependencies, tsc fails (TS2307, TS2304) and
blocks the deploy.

Convert reversi into a real installable PWA

Was failing the new PWA offline correctness check: index.html linked
/manifest.json but vite.config.ts had no VitePWA → service worker was
never registered → installable but couldn't load offline from home
screen. Also referenced /icons/icon-192.png and /icons/icon-512.png
that didn't exist in public/.

Fix mirrors the canonical pattern used in bowling, 2048, etc.:
  - Add vite-plugin-pwa to devDeps; pnpm install regenerates lockfile.
  - Replace vite.config.ts with a full VitePWA setup — proper
    workbox config (raised cap, fonts runtime caching, wasm/json in
    globPatterns), and manifest defined inline so the plugin
    generates manifest.webmanifest at build.
  - Drop the static <link rel="manifest"> from index.html (plugin
    injects its own).
  - Delete web/public/manifest.json (plugin generates).
  - Copy icon-192.png and icon-512.png from the canonical set
    (currently held in bowling).

Preserves theme_color (#2563eb) and background_color (#ffffff)
from the prior manifest.json. Does not touch web/src/App.tsx —
left to a sibling agent's in-flight work.

Make the game actually playable: waits, smarter bots, ippatsu, turn HUD

Four real bugs / UX gaps fixed:

1. **Ippatsu was almost always wrong.** The yaku context used
   `state.turn === player.riichiTurn + 1` — which only matched the *first*
   bot's discard after the declaration, missing the rest of the go-around
   and the riichi-declarer's own next tsumo. Replaced with an explicit
   `ippatsuActive` flag on PlayerState, set true after the declaration
   discard and cleared on the declarer's next discard.

2. **No tenpai / waits indicator.** The player had no way to know whether
   they were one away from winning or which tiles would complete the hand,
   making real play impossible. New `humanWaits(state)` engine function
   plus a TENPAI badge over the hand that renders the waiting tiles as
   small face-up tiles.

3. **Riichi mode was trial-and-error.** Tapping a tile that wouldn't keep
   the hand in tenpai silently did nothing. New `legalRiichiDiscardIndices`
   engine helper; UI dims + disables non-legal tiles while riichi mode is
   armed, and highlights the legal ones with the riichi-yellow outline.

4. **"Your turn" wasn't visible to the player.** Opponents glow when
   active, but the human side had no indicator. Added a YOUR TURN pill
   next to the score badge.

Plus the bot rewrite: replaced the "random with isolated-honor heuristic"
discarder with a per-tile usefulness score
   (same-tile partners + same-suit neighbours +
    kanchan partners − honor/terminal flexibility penalty).
Bots now keep pairs and runs and discard the actually-orphan tile, which
is roughly beginner play. Random bots gave the human winning tiles for
free; this stops that.

Engine tests: 24/24 (added 3: ippatsu default state, humanWaits sanity,
13-tile non-tenpai hand returns no waits). Bundle 69.4 KB gzip.
